title: agents_Inc: Cross-Vendor Governance for an Agentic-AI Workforce
description:
agents_Inc is a Python package that hands work from one AI coding session to other models and checks the result before anyone accepts it. It supports Claude, Codex, Gemini, Mistral and OpenRouter capacity, so you can delegate as you please across subscriptions. A four-rung ladder (Executive, Orchestrator, Workhorse, Grunt) sets the model management. A model never grades its own work: each result passes deterministic checks, then a reviewer, and the decision goes into an append-only ledger. The main entry point is the agents-inc command (dispatch, doctor, repair, ledger). Install with pip install agents-inc, then run agents-inc install; the import name is agents_inc. The project is experimental, and no measurements of efficacy have been benchmarked yet.

This release (0.4.2)

Mostly permission and sandbox fixes for Claude Code sessions, plus the first tooling to measure delegation cost. Patches stay frequent for now.

Added

  • Delegate token usage is kept. agents-inc dispatch saves each Claude delegate's token counts, list-price cost and turn count to usage.json, and agents-inc ledger append fills the ledger's token columns from it.
  • Token bench. tools/delegation_bench.py runs one build-test-verify task under four arms (no delegation, native subagents, agents-inc advisory, agents-inc enforce), each in an isolated home, and scores it with a hidden acceptance script. The size-S fixture ships with it.

Changed

  • The session-start text and the agent nudge say that a named model picks the rung and the route is always agents-inc dispatch. The old wording approved every native subagent on a Claude-only install.
  • The sandboxed-caller fix text (D66, amends D65) names only the sandbox.excludedCommands route, run as one plain command. Auto mode refuses dangerouslyDisableSandbox, and a Codex delegate cannot start inside the sandbox.

Fixed

  • The haiku alias points at claude-haiku-5-5.
  • The Gemini, Mistral and OpenRouter wrappers write temp files under TMPDIR, so they work from a sandboxed macOS session.
  • The token bench runs on macOS: it passes the headless login token to each arm, checks login once per arm, logs install failures, and resolves its output path so arm homes are absolute.
  • The Zenodo record names the PolyForm Small Business 1.0.0 license; 0.4.1 showed CC BY 4.0 by mistake. The no-AI-training term is in the notes and the LICENSE file.

Roadmap at 0.4.2

  • Now: measure the token cost of delegation against doing the work in one session, and fix the remaining permission and sandbox bugs that stop a dispatch from starting.
  • Next: let a Worker launched by a broker lead its own Workers (#73).
  • Later: route work by data classification, so unpublished work reaches only approved providers (#19).

Cite as: DO Mattioli (2026). agents_Inc: Cross-Vendor Governance for an Agentic-AI Workforce. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22670100
